short: The planned schedule of who works which shift.
seoTitle: Shift Roster — Meaning, Formula and Example
metaDescription: A shift roster is the planned schedule of which staff work which hours across a week. The planned schedule of who works which shift.
definition: A shift roster is the planned schedule of which staff work which hours across a week. In hospitality and retail it is the main lever on labour cost, because it decides how staffing matches demand.
bodyHtml:
Why Shift Roster matters

Rostering to headcount rather than to expected demand is how labour cost percentage drifts upward. The waste is rarely dramatic — it is two extra people on a quiet Tuesday, every Tuesday.

Shift Roster formula

Labour hours needed = Forecast covers ÷ Covers served per labour hour

Compare against rostered hours to see the gap.

How Shift Roster works in practice

Build the roster from forecast covers or footfall by day-part, publish it early enough to be fair, and review actual against planned hours weekly. Small mismatches repeated daily are what the monthly number is made of.

faq.question: How far ahead should rosters be published?
faq.answer: At least a week. Late rosters cost goodwill and produce last-minute overtime.

faq.question: How do I know if I am overstaffed?
faq.answer: Compare covers or sales per labour hour across day-parts; the weak slots stand out immediately.

formula.expression: Labour hours needed = Forecast covers ÷ Covers served per labour hour
